To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the catalytic performance of carbon materials in the electron transfer reactions is determined by the electron donor capability of their surface.
MWCNTs with different surface chemistry are effective catalysts for H2O2 degradation and the catalytic performance of MWCNT depends on their electron donor capability.

the catalytic decomposition of H2O 2 is a complex process involving both adsorption and activation of hydrogen peroxide molecules and the rate constant of H2O decomposition is directly proportional to the electron donor capability of carbon materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a theoretical model for the description of the catalytic activity and stability of carbon materials, and it can be used for the design of carbon materials with a predetermined catalytic performance.
the development of the new method for the preparation of the catalysts with controlled surface chemistry.
the catalytic activity and mechanism of carbon nanotube catalysts in the decomposition reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the N-containing C-NT is the most efficient catalyst of H2O(2) decomposition among the studied MWCNTs.
MWCNTs with the highest electron donor capability are the most active catalysts for H2O2 reduction.
the catalytic performance of CNT is mainly determined by its electronic properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the catalytic decomposition of H2O 2 on carbon nanotube is a surface reaction.
carbon nanotubes can be used as catalysts for H2O2 oxidation reactions.
carbon nanotubes are promising materials for the catalytic decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the catalytic performance of carbon materials is not only controlled by the presence of oxygen-containing groups but also by the nature of these groups.
the surface chemistry of carbon nanotube is a key factor in determining their catalytic performance in the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.
the catalytic performance of MWCNT is controlled by the surface chemical composition of the carbon material.
